title: The Notebook They Needed
summaryZh: 谷地要做防洪研究,顧問公司來看了瑪格麗特的三十本筆記,然後說這些資料不能用。兩個星期後,他們又回來了。

sentences.text: By October, Emil was coming up the hill most Saturday mornings.
sentences.zh: 到了十月,艾米爾大部分的星期六早上都會上山。

sentences.text: He had started copying the old notebooks into a spreadsheet on his laptop.
sentences.zh: 他開始把舊筆記本抄進筆電裡的試算表。

sentences.text: He was up to 2003 and it was taking much longer than he had expected.
sentences.zh: 他抄到二〇〇三年,花的時間比他預期的久得多。

sentences.text: Margaret's handwriting from the nineties was small and very neat.
sentences.zh: 瑪格麗特九〇年代的字很小,而且非常工整。

sentences.text: That autumn the council announced a flood study for the whole valley.
sentences.zh: 那年秋天,鎮公所宣布要對整個谷地做防洪研究。

sentences.text: Three houses on the low road had been flooded twice in the last four years.
sentences.zh: 低窪路段上有三戶人家,過去四年淹了兩次水。

sentences.text: A consulting company was hired to work out how high the water could get.
sentences.zh: 鎮公所雇了一間顧問公司,要算出水位可能會漲到多高。

sentences.text: It was Emil's mother who told them about the box on the hill.
sentences.zh: 是艾米爾的媽媽跟他們提起山上那個箱子的。

sentences.text: Two engineers came to the house on a Tuesday and stayed for an hour.
sentences.zh: 星期二,兩位工程師到她家來,待了一個小時。

sentences.text: They took photographs of the box, the gauge, and the ground all around it.
sentences.zh: 他們拍了箱子、雨量筒,還有周圍地面的照片。

sentences.text: They were polite, and they looked at all thirty notebooks.
sentences.zh: 他們很有禮貌,把三十本筆記全都看過了。

sentences.text: The older one explained the problem carefully, so that it would not sound unkind.
sentences.zh: 年長的那位仔細解釋了問題所在,盡量不讓話聽起來刺耳。

sentences.text: The gauge was not a certified instrument and the site had never been inspected.
sentences.zh: 那個雨量筒不是經過認證的儀器,場地也從來沒有被檢查過。

sentences.text: For a study that decided where people could build, that mattered a great deal.
sentences.zh: 對一份要決定哪裡可以蓋房子的研究來說,這件事非常重要。

sentences.text: Margaret said that she understood the problem, and she meant it.
sentences.zh: 瑪格麗特說她理解這個問題,而且是真心的。

sentences.text: She had taught science for twenty-eight years and she knew what a standard was.
sentences.zh: 她教了二十八年自然科學,知道什麼叫做標準。

sentences.text: Emil was a great deal angrier about all of it than she was.
sentences.zh: 艾米爾對這一切生氣的程度,遠遠超過她。

sentences.text: He stopped working on the spreadsheet for almost three weeks.
sentences.zh: 他有將近三個星期沒有再碰那份試算表。

sentences.text: Margaret kept walking up the hill at seven, exactly as before.
sentences.zh: 瑪格麗特照樣每天七點上山,跟以前一模一樣。

sentences.text: In November the older engineer telephoned and asked to come back.
sentences.zh: 十一月,那位年長的工程師打電話來,問能不能再來一趟。

sentences.text: The flood they most needed to understand had happened in September 2004.
sentences.zh: 他們最需要弄清楚的那場水災,發生在二〇〇四年九月。

sentences.text: It was the largest one anybody in the valley could remember.
sentences.zh: 那是谷地裡所有人記憶中最大的一次。

sentences.text: The certified station on the far side of the ridge had only opened in 2009.
sentences.zh: 山脊另一邊那個認證測站,是二〇〇九年才啟用的。

sentences.text: For 2004 it had nothing at all, because in 2004 it did not exist.
sentences.zh: 二〇〇四年它什麼資料都沒有,因為那時候它根本還不存在。

sentences.text: Margaret opened the cupboard in the hall and took out the notebook for that year.
sentences.zh: 瑪格麗特打開走廊上的櫃子,拿出那一年的筆記本。

sentences.text: September the eleventh, 2004: one hundred and six millimetres in a single day.
sentences.zh: 二〇〇四年九月十一日:一天下了一百零六毫米。

sentences.text: The engineer read the line twice and then asked whether she had the days around it.
sentences.zh: 工程師把那一行讀了兩遍,然後問她前後幾天有沒有。

sentences.text: She had them. She had every day of that month, and of every month since 1996.
sentences.zh: 她有。那個月的每一天她都有,而且從一九九六年起每個月都有。

sentences.text: Nobody in the room said anything while the engineer turned the pages.
sentences.zh: 工程師翻頁的時候,房間裡沒有人說話。

sentences.text: The study calls her record an uncertified local series, and uses it anyway.
sentences.zh: 那份研究把她的紀錄稱為「未認證的地方序列」,但還是採用了。

sentences.text: It is written into the report as the only measurement of the 2004 event in the valley.
sentences.zh: 報告裡寫著,這是谷地裡對二〇〇四年那場事件唯一的實測資料。

sentences.text: Nothing about the hill itself has changed since any of that happened.
sentences.zh: 自從那些事發生之後,山上本身什麼都沒有改變。

sentences.text: The box is still white, the pencil is still kept on the shelf inside it.
sentences.zh: 箱子還是白的,鉛筆還是放在裡面的架子上。

sentences.text: Margaret still walks up at seven, and it still takes her longer than it used to.
sentences.zh: 瑪格麗特還是七點上山,還是走得比以前久。

sentences.text: She was not proved right about anything at all, and she does not describe it that way.
sentences.zh: 她並沒有被證明什麼是對的,她自己也不那樣講。

sentences.text: Nobody knew that those numbers would ever be needed, and that is rather the point.
sentences.zh: 沒有人知道那些數字有一天會被需要,而重點大概就在這裡。

sentences.text: Emil has his own key to the box now, and he finished the spreadsheet in March.
sentences.zh: 艾米爾現在有自己那把箱子的鑰匙,試算表也在三月抄完了。

questions.q: Why did the engineers first refuse to use Margaret's records?
options: The gauge was not certified and the site was never inspected
The notebooks were too old to be read clearly
She had missed too many mornings over the years

questions.q: Why did the engineer telephone and come back?
options: The certified station did not exist during the 2004 flood
The council had ordered them to accept local readings
Emil had finished the spreadsheet and sent it to them

questions.q: What does the ending suggest about keeping records?
options: Their value cannot be known at the time they are made
They should always be made with certified instruments
They matter most to the person who writes them
